questions.prompt: Which statement about a linear system x' = Ax + Bu is correct?
options: It can be unstable and still be controllable, and then state feedback can stabilise it.
Poles depend on B, so changing the actuator moves the open-loop poles.
If all poles of A are stable the system is automatically controllable.
Controllable implies stable, because the input can always drive the state to zero.
questions.explanation: Open-loop poles are eigenvalues of A only. Controllability says the input reaches every mode, so feedback can move all poles, including unstable ones.

questions.prompt: A = [[0, 1], [-6, -5]]. What is the pole closest to zero (a real number)?
questions.skillLabel: Poles and stability of a linear model

questions.prompt: For the double integrator x'' = u with state (x, v), which single sensor makes the pair observable?
options: Neither; a double integrator is never observable
Either one alone, since x and v are linked by v = x'
questions.explanation: With C=[1 0], O=[[1,0],[0,1]]. With C=[0 1], CA=[0 0] so position is invisible (a constant offset gives the same velocity record).

questions.prompt: Two identical motors share one command line. The state is the pair of motor speeds. The controllability matrix has rank 1. What does this mean?
options: The rank test was applied to the wrong matrix and says nothing about the system.
The motors are unstable, because the same command drives both with equal gain.
The input can change the average speed but never the difference between the motors.
The sensors are insufficient to reconstruct both speeds from a single measurement.
questions.explanation: The difference of two identical modes is annihilated by the common input: an uncontrollable direction.
questions.skillLabel: Physical meaning of uncontrollable or unobservable modes

questions.prompt: A mobile robot has states (x, y, heading) and only wheel-encoder odometry (distance travelled) as sensor, no compass. Argue whether a linear observer can be built, and what you would add.
rubric: States what observability requires (rank of O) for a model with the encoder output.
Explains that heading/absolute position are unobservable from relative increments.
Proposes a sensor or a model change and a rank check to confirm.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
